name: Light Navy Blue
lede: Light Navy Blue is a mid-dark blue, a sibling of [[light-navy]] that carries the institution word *navy* into a 2010 crowd-survey name rather than a dyer's record.

sections.title: Navy, named for the fleet
sections.body: Navy blue is the dark blue of naval uniforms, which spread to police, postmen and most other uniformed trades between about 1910 and 1950 [3]. This compound simply adds *light* to that root, and our library's only record for the exact name is the xkcd 2010 crowd survey [1]. The library files it as an alternate name of [[newport|Newport]], 2.5 units away, a blue Maerz and Paul record from 1922 [1]. Its other near neighbors are [[dusk-blue]] at 2.8 units and [[denim]] at 3.3, close enough to read as the same blue at a glance [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color within six units of this one, covering at least five percent of the canvas, in 74 of 23,781 paintings, 0.31 percent, as photographed [2]. It is most at home in the 1900s, 26 of the 1,674 paintings we hold from that century, about five times the archive's rate, and inside a painting it most often sits in the mid-tones [2]. The earliest dated match is Giovanni di Paolo's *Adoration of the Magi* of about 1450, centuries before the name; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and a color match is not a pigment test [2].
